# Copilot Instructions

- Before making changes, read the relevant documentation in `docs/` to understand how the system works. Key docs: `docs/ADMIN.md` (admin panel, superuser setup), `docs/AUTHENTICATION.md` (LDAP and dev auth), `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` (startup steps, Docker services), `docs/FAIR_GENOMES.md` (MOLGENIS sync), `docs/STATS.md` (stat definitions and charts), `docs/TICKETING.md` (Alvao integration), `docs/INTERNATIONALIZATION.md` (translations), `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` (workflow and checks). The `README.md` has a project overview, database structure, and environment variable reference.
- Compiled `.mo` files are committed to the repo under `locale/`. When you edit a `.po` file you must also regenerate its `.mo` counterpart by running `python manage.py compilemessages` inside the web container (`./scripts/compose.sh exec web python manage.py compilemessages`), then commit both files together. If the container is not running, start it first with `./scripts/compose.sh up -d db web` and wait for it to be healthy. The container startup script (`docker/startup.py`) also does this automatically on deploy when it detects the `.po` is newer than the `.mo`. The check script (`scripts/check-translations.sh`) enforces that `.mo` files are present and up to date.
- The frontend uses **HTMX 2** for server-driven interactions (form submission, filtering, pagination, cart toggles) and **Alpine.js 3** for client-side UI state (dropdowns, accordions, search filtering, toasts). Both are vendored under `frontend/static/js/` and loaded globally in `base.html`. When adding new interactive behaviour, prefer Alpine `x-data`/`x-show`/`@click` for pure client-side state, and HTMX `hx-get`/`hx-post`/`hx-target` for anything requiring a server round-trip. Avoid adding new vanilla JavaScript files — Alpine and HTMX cover all interactive patterns in the codebase. The only intentional exceptions are `stat-charts.js` (Chart.js canvas rendering, inherently imperative) and `stat_definition_admin.js` (Django admin cascading dropdowns).
- Never add `<script>` blocks with imperative JavaScript logic to templates. For Alpine component logic that cannot fit in a single attribute expression, define a named component via `Alpine.data()` in a static JS file instead. The only permitted inline `<script>` tags are: `<script type="application/json">` data islands (for passing Django template context to Alpine or HTMX), the Tailwind CDN config in `_tailwind_config.html`, and the one-liner hash-scroll helper in `dataset_detail.html`.
- Put all static images (SVG, PNG, JPEG, ICO, WebP) under `frontend/static/img/` and reference them in templates with `<img src="{% static 'img/filename.ext' %}">`. Never place image assets in the project root or outside the `frontend/static/` hierarchy.
- Every user-facing string in templates must be wrapped with `{% trans "…" %}` (or `{% blocktrans %}…{% endblocktrans %}` for multi-word/variable interpolation). After adding new strings, run `python manage.py compilemessages` inside the web container, add translations to both `locale/cs/LC_MESSAGES/django.po` and `locale/en/LC_MESSAGES/django.po`, recompile, and commit all `.po` + `.mo` files together. Strings passed from templates to Alpine components should use the `json_script` data-island pattern or be rendered directly in Django template context rather than as inline JS strings.
- Always use MOU colour tokens for any UI work — never introduce arbitrary hex values or Tailwind default palette colours. The canonical tokens are defined in `frontend/templates/includes/_tailwind_config.html` and are: `mou-cyan` (#53c0d7), `mou-orange` (#f04600), `mou-blue` (#007fc8), `mou-dark` (#1a2332), `mou-yellow` (#fbeebc), `mou-cyan-light` / `mou-cyan-border`, `mou-orange-light` / `mou-orange-border`, `mou-blue-light` / `mou-blue-border`, `page-bg` (#f8f9fa), `outer-bg` (#eef2f7), `site-border` (#e5e7eb), `layer1` / `layer1-border`, `layer2` / `layer2-border`, `txt` (#374151), `txt-muted` (#4b5563). When these tokens are not available (e.g. in JS canvas drawing or inline styles), use the raw hex values from this list.
- Before creating any new HTML, always check `frontend/templates/` for an existing template or include that already provides the needed structure (e.g. cards, modals, tables, form rows, alert banners). Reuse it via `{% extends %}` or `{% include %}` rather than duplicating markup. When adding a new UI pattern that will be used in more than one place, extract it into a reusable partial under `frontend/templates/includes/` so it is not repeated. Never copy-paste blocks of markup between templates — factor shared markup into an include instead.
- Follow a strict **layered architecture** — views (UI layer) must never make direct ORM queries or import Django models. All database access must go through service classes:
  - **Warehouse app**: use `WarehouseMetadataService` (`warehouse/services.py`) for all `metadata_db` and `fair_genomes_db` queries (tables, columns, stat charts, column filters). Use `UnifiedCatalogService` (`shared/services.py`) for cross-database dataset/distribution aggregation.
  - **Ticketing app**: use `TicketingService` (`ticketing/services/ticketing_service.py`) for ticket creation, submission, and history queries. Use `CartService` (`ticketing/cart.py`) for session-based cart operations.
  - **Views may only** import from service modules, DTOs (`shared/dtos.py`), export helpers (`shared/export.py`), and cart utilities — never from `*.models` directly.
  - **Admin files and management commands** are exempt from this rule — they may use direct ORM access and model imports.
  - When adding new database queries, add a method to the appropriate service class rather than querying in the view. Service methods should return plain Python data structures (dicts, lists, dataclasses), not QuerySets.
- After making any code changes, run the full quality check suite via `./scripts/check.sh` (or `./scripts/check.sh --check` for CI-style dry-run). This runs linting (Ruff), formatting (Ruff), type checking (mypy), security scanning (Bandit), translation completeness, the test suite, and a Docker build check. Fix all reported issues before considering the task complete. Individual checks can also be run separately: `scripts/check-lint.sh`, `scripts/check-format.sh`, `scripts/check-types.sh`, `scripts/check-security.sh`, `scripts/check-translations.sh`, `scripts/check-tests.sh`, `scripts/check-docker.sh`. Tests can also be run inside the container with `./scripts/compose.sh exec web python manage.py test`.
